recent_posts.title: Long Live The Cyberdeck #piday #raspberrypi
recent_posts.summary: Cyberdecks — custom-built portable computers often powered by Raspberry Pi — are gaining mainstream media attention via viral short-form videos, with CNN and Yahoo! covering the trend. The movement is framed as a counter-cultural response to homogenized, corporate tech design. Raspberry Pi highlighted favorite community builds on their blog, and Adafruit promotes their CYBERDECK HAT and CYBERDECK Bonnet accessories for Raspberry Pi 400 and 500.

recent_posts.title: How to Display the Weather
recent_posts.summary: A brief post from Adafruit pointing makers to their Learning System resources for building a weather display project. It highlights CircuitPython as a tool for programming microcontrollers and links to community resources including Discord, YouTube shows, and newsletters.

recent_posts.title: NEW GUIDE: ESP-NOW Walkie Talkies #AdafruitLearningSystem @Adafruit
recent_posts.summary: A new Adafruit Learning System guide shows how to build a pair of walkie talkies using the Feather ESP32-S3 Reverse TFT board. The project uses the ESP-NOW wireless protocol with Arduino code to send and receive I2S audio packets of up to 10 seconds each. A w.FL antenna extends the communication range for both indoor and outdoor use.

recent_posts.title: Making an ESP32 device which connects to Claude over Bluetooth
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic's Claude for macOS and Windows now supports Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) connectivity, allowing makers to build hardware devices that integrate with Claude Cowork and Claude Code. As a demonstration, a desk pet was built on an ESP32 (M5StickCPlus) that reacts to Claude sessions — sleeping when idle, waking on session start, showing impatience when approval prompts are pending, and allowing approve/deny actions directly from the device. The firmware uses the Arduino framework and the M5StickCPlus library for display, IMU, and button drivers.

recent_posts.title: The Orange Pi 6 Plus – a review and benchmarks
recent_posts.summary: A detailed review of the Orange Pi 6 Plus single-board computer featuring the CIX P1 chip with 12 CPU cores, Mali G720 GPU, dedicated NPU, and dual 5GbE. The reviewer spent months testing the board, diving deep into boot chains, vendor GPU blobs, and AI inference runtimes. While the GPU and NPU stack work and local AI inference is achievable, power consumption and fan noise are higher than expected for the form factor. Compared to Rockchip-based boards, the software experience is more polished, and the reviewer was able to run useful workloads using a custom OS image.

recent_posts.title: From AI slop to AI empowerment: raising the bar for open-source contributions
recent_posts.summary: Tom Stavert of Scott Logic discusses the growing challenge of AI-generated code in open-source contributions. Common red flags include emoji-heavy PR descriptions, unusual library imports, overly verbose variable names, and excessive unit tests. The core concern is that contributors often cannot explain AI-generated code when questioned during review. The key recommendation is that contributors should spend at least as much time reviewing AI-generated code as a reviewer would — and be fully prepared to answer questions about every line they submit.

recent_posts.title: Tracking down a 25% regression on LLVM RISC-V
recent_posts.summary: A deep-dive into a ~25% performance regression on RISC-V targets introduced by an LLVM commit that improved isKnownExactCastIntToFP. The optimization folded fpext(sitofp x to float) to double into a direct uitofp x to double cast, but inadvertently broke a downstream narrowing optimization in visitFPTrunc. This caused the compiler to emit fdiv.d (33-cycle latency) instead of fdiv.s (19-cycle latency) on RISC-V. The fix extends getMinimumFPType with range analysis to recognize that fptrunc(uitofp x double) to float can be reduced to uitofp x to float, restoring the narrowing optimization.

recent_posts.title: Bulgaria's Apple II clone and the story of Cold War computing
recent_posts.summary: A personal account of Bulgaria's Правец (Pravetz) computers — Apple II clones built behind the Iron Curtain. In 1979, engineer Ivan Marangozov at Sofia's Institute of Technical Cybernetics and Robotics built the IMKO-1, a near-identical clone of the Apple II with the same ROM, schematics, and 6502 CPU running at 1 MHz. Key differences included a heavy metal case, a linear power supply, and Cyrillic characters replacing lowercase Latin. The Правец 82 became a staple in Bulgarian schools, representing a fascinating chapter in Cold War computing history.

recent_posts.title: The 192 MHz WCH CH32V205 RISC-V MCU offers a 480 Mbps USB 2.0 interface
recent_posts.summary: WCH has released the CH32V205, a 32-bit RISC-V microcontroller running at up to 192 MHz with 32KB SRAM and 256KB flash. Its standout feature is a USB 2.0 high-speed interface with a 480 Mbps PHY, alongside a full-speed USB 2.0 port, USB-C PD support, 80 GPIOs, a 16-channel 12-bit ADC, touchkey interface, and connectivity options including CAN Bus, USART, I2C, SPI, and QSPI. It builds on the earlier CH32V203 with expanded GPIO, faster USB, and USB-C PD. English datasheets are available, and development can be done via MoonRiver IDE or the CH32fun GCC toolchain, which may soon add support for this new MCU.

recent_posts.title: CircuitPython 10.2.0-rc.0 Released!
recent_posts.summary: CircuitPython 10.2.0-rc.0 is a release candidate for the next stable minor version. Key highlights include a new audiotools.SpeedChanger, qspibus support for displayio, USB SD card stability improvements, a merge of MicroPython v1.27, an update to ESP-IDF v5.5.3, and significant additions to the Zephyr port including simulated hardware testing. Several new boards are supported including Pimoroni Badger2350, TinyCircuits Thumby, and Waveshare ESP32-S3 Touch AMOLED. Known issues include CIRCUITPY drive problems on some STM32 boards.
